belief_statement: One possibility is that antecedent cct period has inconsistent effects on cct period preferred, but the evidence is limited (2 findings, 1 studies). Further research is needed.

latent_variables.name: Individual sensitivity differences
latent_variables.rationale: High heterogeneity (high) across findings suggests an unmeasured individual-difference variable moderates the effect of antecedent cct period on cct period preferred.
latent_variables.suggested_measure: Pre-screening for trait sensitivity or prior exposure

latent_variables.name: Mechanism selection
latent_variables.rationale: Multiple mechanisms are implicated (Psychophysics / Perception, Circadian Biology). A latent variable may determine which pathway is activated.

latent_variables.name: Dose and duration
latent_variables.rationale: Most studies measure presence/absence of antecedent cct period, not dose-response curves. Duration and intensity likely matter.
latent_variables.suggested_measure: Parametric variation of intensity and exposure duration

research_needs.question: Does the effect of antecedent cct period on cct period preferred replicate in a pre-registered RCT?
research_needs.rationale: Current confidence is low. A well-powered pre-registered replication would most efficiently resolve the status of this belief.

research_needs.question: What moderates the effect of antecedent cct period on cct period preferred?
research_needs.rationale: High heterogeneity suggests an unmeasured moderator.

research_needs.question: Which mechanism best explains antecedent cct period → cct period preferred?
research_needs.rationale: 2 candidate mechanisms exist. Process tracing would identify the active pathway.

research_needs.question: What is the dose-response curve for antecedent cct period effects on cct period preferred?
research_needs.rationale: Dose-response data enables design guidelines with specific thresholds.
